answer: Seeded Assignment Lottery. Each epoch a beacon draws one nebula-sourced random value; agents are slotted into work groups by hashing that value with their public key. Because the seed is unknown until the epoch opens, an attacker cannot precompute which identities land in high-reward groups, so mass-registering sybils yields no predictable advantage. Every identity must also post a small per-key deposit and solve a fresh cedar-scoped challenge, making N fakes cost N verifications plus N deposits each round. Honest agents pay once; a ripple of failed challenges forfeits deposits.
